comments.author: pjmlp
comments.story: Super Monkey Ball ported to a website
comments.why: Infinity Blade as showcase of mobile OpenGL capability
comments.text: Fast forward to 2026 and after 15 years, the browser vendors have not yet provided anything remotely similar to RenderDoc, only SpectorJS survives, barely usable. Also this game remains the exception, Infinity Blade was released in 2010 to show what iPhone could do with OpenGL ES 3.0, the base for WebGL 2.0, and yet most Web games are basically Flash like remakes. [LINK] "Infinity Blade: iPhone Trailer", 15 years ago [VIDEO]

comments.author: pjmlp
comments.story: Terraria developer bashes Unity, donates $200k to open source alternatives
comments.why: Benchmark of graphics WebGL games have not matched
comments.text: If they only care about 2011 (WebGL) or 2015 (WebGPU) hardware, sure. Still waiting to see a WebGL game that matches Infinity Blade, released in 2011 alongside iPhone 3G and iPhone 4. Trailer: [VIDEO] Meaning, those graphic API are able to deliver at least PS 3 graphics, yet due to browser support, specially the way browsers blacklist drivers, download sizes, and lack of tooling on par with native, very few professional developers bother, hence streaming.
